articles.summary: 11/23/26 Semrush’s New Topics Layer Helps Marketers Measure Brand Visibility Across Google and AI Search In One View Topics combine Semrush’s 29B+ keywords and 317M+ AI prompts so marketers can see their visibility across a cluster of relevant queries. A new AI-influenced traffic metric shows how AI visibility converts into website visits. Ask any marketer today and they’ll tell you that growing brand visibility in AI search is top of mind. Yet most marketing teams right now are juggling keyword lists in one dashboard while tracking isolated AI prompts in another, which doubles the work and fragments reporting. Meanwhile, connected visibility growth happens at the topic level, where AI assistants evaluate trusted authority to make recommendations. To build lasting visibility for human searchers and AI engines alike, marketers should anchor their search strategy around whole topic clusters, instead of pursuing individual AI prompts or keywords alone. Semrush’s new Topics layer helps marketers optimize and measure their brand visibility across SEO and AI search in one connected view. It brings together Semrush’s expansive search intelligence of more than 29 billion keywords and over 317 million AI prompts so marketers can track how their brand performs across whole topics in Google and AI search, including ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Plus, a new AI-influenced traffic metric in Semrush now helps marketers measure how visibility in AI answers leads to website visits later – a crucial piece to measuring the impact of their strategy. Until now, marketers have had to chase AI visibility one prompt at a time, separately from their SEO data. This disjointed view rarely gives the business a clear answer on how discoverable their brand is in AI platforms. By bringing SEO and AI search together at the topic level in Semrush, and introducing a new metric that estimates AI-influenced traffic, we’re helping teams see where to invest and prove the ROI of their brand visibility efforts. -Vitalii Obishchenko, VP, Software Development, Adobe One View Of Everything That Buyers Search and Ask The buyer journey is expanding, going far beyond a single search box. Buyers move between Google and AI assistants, and the results they see are increasingly personalized. A Semrush analysis found that U.S. users of major LLMs are spending about ten minutes per session in 2026, signifying a seismic shift in consumer behavior compared to traditional search. It also represents an opportunity for brands to find buyers where they’re searching, increasingly within AI platforms. Whether a brand gets recommended in AI search now depends on its relevance and authority across a whole topic, not its rank for one keyword or its mention in just one prompt. Marketers can use a topic to measure total search demand and competitive visibility across both search keywords and AI prompts, instead of relying on keyword volume alone. Plus, Topics brings both AI search and SEO data into one unified view, giving marketers a fuller picture of how their brand competes for visibility across search and AI. For example, a marketer for a skincare brand can track the topic ‘sensitive skincare’ to capture Google keywords like ‘moisturizer for sensitive skin’, as well as relevant AI prompts such as ‘what skincare routine works for my sensitive skin?’ Topics in Semrush reveals where the brand leads in Google, how it shows up in AI answers, and where its competitor compares across both. Semrush’s new Topics tool measures what matters to us now: how much of a topic we own, not where one keyword ranks. My team uses it for measurement, which is top of mind for leadership. And it’s also been a helpful tool for where we go next: content planning, internal linking and a whole lot more. -Rob Peck, Director of PPC and SEO, Mambo Media Finally, A Metric To Measure The Value Of AI Visibility Although most teams agree that AI search is important for brand discovery, marketers have struggled to demonstrate the return on their AI search efforts – until now. The new AI-influenced traffic metric estimates the traffic a brand gets when it’s mentioned or cited prominently in a topic’s AI answers, whether that traffic comes as direct visits, branded organic searches or AI referral clicks. It highlights traffic that standard analytics tools can’t currently attribute: visits that started with an AI recommendation rather than a search click. Semrush has also updated the way organic traffic from SERP position and search volume is estimated to reflect how click-through rates on Google have changed this year. The new CTR model takes more features of today’s SERPs into account, including search intent, branded versus non-branded keywords, SERP features, zero-click signals, and the impact of AI Overviews and AI Mode. The result is a more accurate estimate of the traffic a ranking position is likely to drive today. Availability The topics layer is rolling out across Semrush products from mid-November, starting with: Organic Rankings 2.0: A topic-level view of visibility across Google and AI search combined. It shows how fully a brand covers a topic compared to other industry players, and where AI systems are already citing competitors instead. Keyword Magic Tool 2.0: A redesigned keyword research tool with a new algorithm. It finds relevant keywords and prompts based on SERP and semantic similarity instead of keyword stemming, so they’re grouped by what they mean, not how they’re spelled. These reports are also available within Organic Rankings and Keyword & Prompt Research on the Semrush Enterprise platform. Topics will launch first in the US and UK, and then roll out to additional markets. Semrush plans to bring topic-level data and insights to more tools and reports, with more releases to follow. This unified view is also coming soon to Adobe Brand Visibility.
articles.title: Semrush’s New Topics Layer Helps Marketers Measure Brand Visibility Across Google and AI Search In One View

He was stuck in Lagos traffic on his way to the National Theatre. With time running out, he stopped a soldier on his bike and negotiated a price to the venue. He arrived tense, with three minutes to explain years of work. By the time he finished, he was convinced he had done badly. It was a familiar feeling for Caleb. He had already faced more than 100 rejections that year. This was his third attempt at the competition. But Caleb has learnt something about rejection. When one opportunity doesn’t work out, he moves on to the next. Our latest Founders Spotlight features Caleb Iwuoha, founder of Acecore. His company makes clean energy hardware and came from personal loss, hard choices, and people who chose to stay. The day everything changed On June 13, 2024, Caleb’s father went in for cancer surgery. During the operation, the hospital lost power. Caleb says the outage contributed to a medical error. His father died in December that year. Caleb had already made up his mind about building clean energy products in Nigeria. COVID-19 had shown him the risks of relying on imported equipment. But losing his father made the problem much more personal. He knew what unreliable power could cost a business. Now, he had experienced what could happen when the power went out during a medical procedure.Losing his father gave him another reason to keep building. Why starting in Port Harcourt mattered to him Caleb knew that Lagos offered better access to investors and startup networks. He still chose to build Acecore in Port Harcourt.He wanted talented people in Rivers State to find jobs close to home. He also believed that a company making hardware didn’t need to be based in Lagos to succeed. There was another reason he had to make do with what was available. He had no money to set up a factory, so he started in his father’s garage. Caleb began researching the business during his industrial training year in 2021. He launched the brand in 2022, while he was still a student. He had no savings, no revenue, and little experience running a company. Later, Acecore secured funding. He expanded the factory into the family compound. The factory had grown, but building hardware in Nigeria brought new problems. The people who believed enough to stay. At some point, Caleb began asking himself why he had chosen such a difficult business. Hardware took time and money to build. Finding the right engineers was another challenge. Skilled hardware engineers were much harder to find than software engineers and when the company wasn’t making money, some people left. He remembers one hardware engineer who decided to quit. Caleb offered to change his contract. He was willing to meet whatever terms would make the engineer stay. The engineer still left. Caleb had to find another way to keep the work going, so he started learning more of the technical work himself. He began doing the coding, design, and manufacturing work himself. But not everyone walked away. One of his co-founders left a paying job in Lagos and moved to Port Harcourt to build Acecore. Another turned down an opportunity to travel abroad. Caleb said some of his admin staff worked for four years without pay. Other team members made difficult choices too. Caleb says his chief software engineer turned down opportunities at Google and Facebook. His finance lead, Colin, also passed on roles at major Nigerian energy companies. He also postponed plans to pursue a PhD at MIT so he could continue building the company. He describes the kind of people willing to take these risks as “crazy.” But he speaks about them with gratitude. He said his faith and co-founder kept him going. When we asked how he keeps people committed to the work, Caleb pointed to leading by example. He recalls working through three nights at the factory without sleep. He wanted his engineers to see the standard of work he expected from them.It was an exhausting way to work, and the company’s problems didn’t disappear overnight. Still, he had people around him who continued to believe they could make it work. What 100 rejections taught him Caleb’s approach to rejection started long before his TechCabal win. His response has become almost routine. When an application fails, he doesn’t spend the rest of the day thinking about it. He looks for the next opportunity and applies again. articles.summary: Global randomized trial enrolled 960 patients over 13 monthsBoxX-NoAF is designed to evaluate whether concomitant surgical ablation and left atrial appendage exclusion can reduce post-operative and longer-term atrial fibrillation in cardiac surgery patients, with primary study results expected to be presented in mid-2027.MASON, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 23, 2026--AtriCure, Inc. (Nasdaq: ATRC), a leading innovator in surgical treatments and therapies for atrial fibrillation (Afib), left atrial appendage (LAA) management, and post-operative pain management, today announced the completion of enrollment in the Box Lesion Creation with Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion to Reduce the Occurrence of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation (BoxX-NoAF) clinical trial (NCT06989775). The trial enrolled 960 patients across participating centers worldwide and is designed to evaluate whether surgical ablation combined with LAA exclusion can reduce the occurrence of post-operative and longer-term atrial fibrillation in elevated-risk cardiac surgery patients.The BoxX-NoAF trial is a foundational strategic initiative for AtriCure to expand the clinical and economic value proposition of its surgical ablation and LAA management technologies through high-quality randomized clinical evidence."Completing enrollment in BoxX-NoAF marks an important milestone and positions the trial as a meaningful upcoming catalyst," said Michael Carrel, President and Chief Executive Officer of AtriCure. "Together with LeAAPS, BoxX-NoAF advances our long-term clinical evidence strategy and reinforces AtriCure's leadership position in surgical therapies designed to improve outcomes for cardiac surgery patients. We believe successful outcomes will strengthen the evidence supporting our EnCompass and AtriClip platforms, creating additional growth opportunities through expanding treatment options for indicated cardiac surgery patients at risk of post-operative atrial fibrillation."“Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is one of the most common and consequential complications after cardiac surgery,” said Richard Whitlock, MD, PhD, FRCSC, Cardiothoracic Surgeon, McMaster University, and Global Principal Investigator. “We believe that combining a box lesion with left atrial appendage (LAA) exclusion during surgery could meaningfully reduce the incidence of new-onset POAF and alleviate its many associated burdens, including stroke, longer hospital stays, and death. The BoxX-NoAF trial is yet another study that sets precedent regarding the execution of well-powered, methodologically robust studies to answer important questions in our field.”Post-operative atrial fibrillation is among the most common complications following cardiac surgery and is associated with increased morbidity, longer hospital stays, higher healthcare costs, and greater risk of future atrial fibrillation. Despite its prevalence, no FDA-approved therapy currently exists specifically for the reduction of post-operative and longer-term clinical Afib in this patient population. BoxX-NoAF was designed to evaluate a potential approach to address this significant unmet need.With enrollment complete, the study moves into its next phase, which includes ongoing patient follow-up, data collection, monitoring, and statistical analysis. Clinical data from participating sites are currently being aggregated and validated. AtriCure currently expects primary study results to be presented in mid-2027.The company expects data from BoxX-NoAF, together with results from its broader portfolio of clinical programs, to further inform future treatment guidelines and regulatory submissions.About BoxX-NoAFBoxX-NoAF is a prospective, multicenter, randomized clinical trial conducted under an FDA-approved investigational device exemption (IDE) evaluating the use of the AtriCure Isolator® Synergy™ EnCompass® Clamp together with the AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System to reduce the occurrence of new-onset atrial fibrillation, including long-term atrial fibrillation, in elevated-risk cardiac surgery patients. The study enrolled 960 patients at participating centers worldwide. The use of these devices for this indication is investigational, and their safety and effectiveness for this use have not been established. For more information about BoxX-NoAF, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06989775About AtriCureAtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 59 million people worldwide. Surgeons around the globe use AtriCure technologies for the treatment of Afib, reduction of Afib-related complications, and post-operative pain management. AtriCure’s Isolator® Synergy™ Ablation System is the first medical device to receive FDA approval for the treatment of persistent and long-standing persistent Afib. AtriCure’s AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System products are the most widely sold LAA management devices worldwide. AtriCure’s Hybrid AF™ Therapy is a minimally invasive procedure that provides a lasting solution for long-standing persistent Afib patients. AtriCure’s cryoICE cryoSPHERE® and cryoXT® probes are cleared for temporary ablation of peripheral nerves to block pain, providing pain relief in cardiac, thoracic and amputation procedures. articles.summary: ReNew calls for responsible, community-focused data centres in India, prioritising zero water, clean energy, and domestic manufacturing expansion, says Vaishali Nigam Sinha ReNew Energy Global Plc, a leading decarbonisation solutions company, has recently announced a major expansion of its clean energy and manufacturing footprint in Andhra Pradesh, with a focus on data centre infrastructure, backward integration in solar manufacturing and rare-earth permanent magnet production. Company’s Co-Founder and Chairperson (Sustainability) Vaishali Nigam Sinha is excited particularly about entering the rapidly evolving data centre landscape, but at the same time aware of the duty to comply with the relevant ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) framework. Speaking to The Hindu on the sidelines of an industry event at the CII Partnership Summit-2026, Ms. Sinha said that ReNew was supplying a substantial portion of its clean energy to data centres, and it factored in ‘responsible governance’ as critical to the sector's expansion. She emphasised that India needs ‘responsible data centres’ that care for the communities in which they operate and give back to them, by trying to embed zero water, zero noise, and clean energy technologies to the extent possible. “The country really needs data centres because the Fourth Industrial Revolution is not going to wait for us,” she observed. She said that ReNew was in the process of integrating its supply chain upwards in the renewables sector (integrating ingots, silicon and polysilicon). She said that ReNew was in the process of integrating its supply chain upwards in the renewables sector (integrating ingots, silicon and polysilicon). Air-cooling systems On public and regulatory concerns surrounding water consumption by large data centres, ReNew CEO Sanjay Varghese said air-cooling systems must be the way forward as they help reduce water requirements by half or more. Though air-cooling is relatively expensive, it accounts for a small fraction of the huge capital expenditure being incurred on data centres, he noted, suggesting that desalination should be undertaken as a long-term solution along with air cooling, especially in water-sensitive areas. Renewable energy Ms. Sinha described the renewable energy sector's current hurdles, such as securing land, talent, and faster execution, as ‘good problems’ driven by rapid growth and constructive public-policy engagement. She said ReNew laid greater focus on domestic R&D and equipment manufacturing to achieve the much-needed self-reliance, as though raw materials were available globally, refining capacity and capital equipment manufacturing were heavily concentrated in China. Mr. Varghese stated that ReNew was now producing solar modules and cells and setting up ingot and wafer manufacturing. The next phase involves backward integration into high-purity polysilicon made from domestically available quartz to eliminate import dependence. He pointed out that ReNew has recently won a government tender to manufacture rare-earth permanent magnets, an indispensable part of electric mobility.

These grants were made pursuant to the company’s 2021 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan, were approved by the compensation committee of the board of directors pursuant to a delegation by the company’s board of directors, and were made as a material inducement to such employees’ acceptance of employment with the company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) as a component of his or her employment compensation. The RSUs vest over four years, with 25 percent of such RSUs vesting when such employee completes 12 months of continuous service measured from the vesting commencement date, and the balance of the RSUs vesting in a series of successive equal yearly installments of 1/4 of the original number of RSUs upon each such employee’s completion of each additional year
articles.title: Schrödinger Reports Inducement Grants under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)

articles.summary: Monro, Inc. (Nasdaq: MNRO), a leading provider of automotive repair and tire services, today announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has elected not to declare a cash dividend for the third quarter and to suspend future dividends until further action of the Board as the Company continues to execute its performance improvement plan, amid ongoing challenges in the macro-environment. The Company continues to maintain adequate liquidity to fund its operations and invest in its initiatives including, among other things, driving profitable customer acquisition and activation, improving store-based customer experience and selling effectiveness, and increasing merchandising productivity. The Board is continuing to evaluate a broad range of strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value, as previously announced.
